entries.title: Lazy Quick Paste engine per opening with retirement
entries.invariant: Create on demand, dispose Dart owners and native engine on retirement; preserve focus and paste behavior. macOS and Windows share one in-process lifecycle: each opening without a live context starts a quickPasteMain engine that owns one QuickPasteController; Dart signals ready after its first page, native sends opened, reveals only after the present acknowledgement, retires on the next main-loop turn once the popup is hidden with no live presentation, and stops the engine after the acknowledged shutdown or a 1 s failsafe. Dart shutdown awaits an in-flight activation before acknowledging, so a started Copy completes and releases its watch lease; native replies to paste before scheduling retirement, so a completed paste is never delayed, and the failsafe bounds any slower Copy. A reopening before retirement reuses only that not-yet-retired context. Windows no longer retains a hidden engine with per-opening controllers. Linux still runs Quick Paste as a separate process that attaches to the runtime endpoint and exits on idle. Standard keyboard and native window close use the existing cancellation/hide/retirement paths. macOS Command-W and Option-Command-W invalidate the popup paste session before acknowledged retirement. Windows preserves the native system-menu close command. Linux GTK close/iconify coalesces duplicate requests, cancels/restores the transaction, and exits on idle; its callback is owned and released by the GTK window. Quit from the Linux popup requests primary-process termination through PID/transaction authorization. No event monitor, polling timer, retained presentation, or engine prewarming is introduced.
entries.next_step: Measure startup latency, peak and recovered memory for 100 open/close cycles; compare reuse only with evidence. Windows engine-per-opening retirement has no native build, interaction, latency or resource evidence yet. Moving Linux to the same in-process model requires replacing the child-PID D-Bus authorization of the Wayland transaction and the Linux native qualification evidence that requires a distinct quick_paste_pid; Linux evidence for either model is unresolved.

entries.title: Persist unchanged authenticated peer profiles at most once per half TTL
entries.invariant: Every session and probe records the authenticated profile in memory at its exact observation time. entries.title: Schedule reachability renewal by deadline instead of a 1 Hz tick
entries.invariant: The reachability monitor sleeps until the earliest renewal is due, a new observation is recorded, or a bounded recheck elapses for peers without dial candidates. Probe freshness, renewal lead and offline retry cadence are unchanged, and renewal batches never start closer than one second apart. Unmeasured presence is measured as soon as the monitor wakes, except for a peer whose last probe authenticated but was not acknowledged: it stays Online and is renewed no sooner than the 10-second failure freshness, whatever presence arrives meanwhile, until any other probe outcome. Previously such a peer was re-probed at the one-second batch floor.

entries.title: Defer background dials and probes to a version-incompatible peer
entries.invariant: An authenticated peer that proves to speak another protocol version, by declaring it or by closing without replying to the first message while its advertisement or last authenticated profile names another version, is shown as a version mismatch and left alone by scheduled sessions and reachability probes for five minutes, each new mismatch restarting the wait. Compatibility evidence ends the wait at once, explicit sync still dials, and no protocol check is relaxed. Previously such a peer was dialled every scheduler round (10 s) and probed about once per second.

entries.title: One synchronized version per organization record id
entries.invariant: An organization record id lives only in organization_records. Record copies that builds without organization records stored as ordinary clips are adopted (when no record holds the id) and removed from the clipboard history before pins are seeded, found by one primary-key range seek. Previously a seeded or received record left the id in both tables, so a peer advertised two versions of it and served whichever row the read returned first: the receiver dropped every such item as not matching its summary, re-requested it every round (about 9 items per session on the reporting Mac), and its receive cursor never advanced past them.

entries.title: No per-session resend of tombstones for leftover pin stamps
entries.invariant: P2P planning requests a version for its pin state only when both the local and remote versions are live, matching apply, which never stores pin state on or from a tombstone. A deleted pinned item's tombstone keeps its pin stamp on the deleting device, but it is transferred once and then no longer re-sent and declined every session.

entries.title: Storage usage readout from the quota's own index
entries.invariant: The used-of-quota readout is the byte sweep's own total (covering scan of idx_items_unpinned_bytes over live unpinned rows) plus one idx_items_evictable seek for the oldest unpinned capture time; no payload or table row is read and no counter, column or migration is added. It is computed only for a settings reply (GetConfig, SetConfig) and carried there, so it adds no request to settings loads and nothing to status, events or captures. The application re-reads it after a history change only while the readout has a listener, with one request in flight and one trailing read per burst; the header cell listens only in the stages that show it (not in the bottom-navigation header) and the Settings row only while Settings is presented; there is no timer, and an unreadable store reports no value rather than zero.

entries.title: History group counts from covering indexes
entries.invariant: The pinned count and one count per displayed day are exact and read from covering indexes in one snapshot: idx_items_history for pins, one idx_items_evictable range per client-supplied [from, before) instant pair, with origin and source-application filters answered by idx_items_syncable and idx_items_source_app seeks and tag filters by the tag tables. No table row, payload or FTS text is read, at most 256 ranges are accepted, and rows outside the requested groups are not visited. A query with text search, a content-class or a semantic-kind filter is answered as uncounted instead of estimated, because those columns follow the encrypted payload in the row. The application asks only when group headers are enabled, for days in resident pages, when the query, the displayed days or the history changes; one request is in flight, an uncountable query is asked once, and counts are withheld while a displayed page reports undecryptable rows. There is no timer.

entries.title: Streamed text export and progress-reporting backup
entries.invariant: The app's text export reads history in one snapshot and hands it over in chunks of about 1 MiB through a one-frame queue, and the client appends each chunk to a same-directory temporary file, so no process holds the whole export or its pretty-printed copy; the single-reply export it replaces held the whole export (up to the 32 MiB frame) in the daemon reply and twice in the client. Backup uses SQLite's online backup in 256-page steps. Progress for both is sent at most every 250 ms and only while an operation runs; nothing polls.

entries.title: One wall-clock deadline task with resume sweeps
entries.invariant: Every feature deadline (item expiry, paste-queue idle stop and undo, import and rule-preview plans, MCP session expiry) goes through one deadline task per runtime. It holds a timer only for the earliest deadline due within 1 h; later deadlines and an empty schedule hold no timer. Long-horizon deadlines are swept at task start, on resume, on sync receipt (coalesced into the 500 ms library flush) and on the first request after 15 quiet minutes, which covers the Android foreground and IME-only processes without an alarm. Resume signals: the macOS wake notification, Windows PowerRegisterSuspendResumeNotification and Linux logind PrepareForSleep. A 60 s re-arm cap applies only when the resume subscription failed and a short-horizon deadline exists.

entries.title: Read-time expiry filtering without an Android alarm job
entries.invariant: History, search, list and every surface built on them filter rows whose expires_at has passed at read time, through the partial index on clip_local_state(expires_at), so a late purge never shows an expired item. The purge runs from the deadline sweep only while a runtime is running; Android schedules no alarm or job for expiry, and nothing runs when no expiring item exists.

entries.invariant: The rule set is compiled into one immutable evaluator per rules revision and shared by every capture until a Library rules change invalidates it. Detection runs only when an enabled rule needs a detected kind, and regular expressions only for enabled rules. Detection reads at most a 64 KiB prefix and regex conditions at most a 1 MiB prefix; regex programs are capped at 512 KiB and their lazy DFA at 1 MiB, with no backreferences or look-around.

entries.invariant: Items received through sync are evaluated for protection actions (secret mask, hide from AI, expiry) and auto-tags with the same compiled evaluator as local captures, inside the apply transaction. entries.invariant: Queue entries reference history items by id; shared and selected text is captured into history first, and a sealed snapshot is stored only for rendered snippet output. entries.invariant: Snippet search reads the snippets projection and its FTS table, never decrypting organization records per query. Templates are parsed once per revision into a cache of at most 32 entries that is dropped by SnippetOp::Release when a surface closes (Settings section detach, Quick Paste presentation end, IME panel hide). entries.invariant: A peer whose device profile has no organization_kinds is offered only legacy organization records (kind_class = 1), served by idx_organization_kind_versions, so an older peer never receives and re-requests records it would decline every session. After an upgrade, a cursor stored without organization_kinds is reset once, costing one full summary re-exchange per peer.

entries.title: Coalesced library and progress events; MCP ignores copy events
entries.invariant: Library change events are coalesced to at most one per 500 ms window and progress events to one per operation per 250 ms. Watchers subscribe with WatchEvents to the kinds they need; the MCP CLI subscribes only to AI approval, grant and status events, so a copy never wakes it. An MCP session ends with its watch connection, and unattached or idle sessions expire through the deadline task. The app's approval listener reuses the shared event stream and reads pending approvals only on approval events and once at start.

entries.title: One import plan and one rule-preview plan, released promptly
entries.invariant: At most one snippet import plan and one rule-preview plan exist per runtime. A plan holds ids and effects only, and is released by commit or apply, by cancel (the preview dialog sends Cancel with its request id on close), by a newer plan of the same kind, or by a 10-minute deadline. A rule preview examines at most 1,000 items in batches of 50 and holds one decrypted text at a time.

entries.title: Installed applications load only while the application picker is open
entries.owner_module: copypaste-source-app installed applications and the Flutter application picker
entries.invariant: The installed-application list (at most 1,024 entries, names and identifiers only) is read when the picker opens and dropped when it closes. Icons are rendered on demand for visible rows at 64 px and 32 KiB at most, are never cached natively, and are memoized only by the view that requested them; misses are retried after a minute and the History source-app list is held only while a lookup runs. On Windows one uninstall-registry listing (at most 1,024 entries with executable paths) answers listing, lookups and icons for 30 seconds and is dropped on the next call after that; the daemon capture path never scans uninstall registrations. Nothing is loaded by the daemon. The Android worker queues at most 64 requests, pending icon renders are dropped when the picker closes, and its thread exits after 30 idle seconds.
